title: Lahaina, Hawaii Travel Guide

hero.headline: Lahaina, Hawaii Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Context on Lahaina's harbor history, landmarks, and coastal setting on West Maui.

overview: Lahaina is a historic town on the west coast of Maui that served as the Hawaiian Kingdom capital from 1820 to 1845. It later developed as a whaling port and commercial harbor, and many surviving landmarks document that period. The district sits on a dry leeward shoreline with direct access to marine channels between Maui, Lanai, and Molokai. Trip planning often focuses on historic sites, waterfront infrastructure, and regional ferry or excursion access.

highlights.title: Former royal capital
highlights.description: Lahaina held administrative importance in the early nineteenth-century Hawaiian Kingdom.

highlights.title: Whaling-era harbor town
highlights.description: The waterfront and preserved structures reflect Lahaina's role in Pacific maritime trade.

thingsToDo.title: Lahaina Historic District
thingsToDo.description: The Lahaina Historic District includes buildings and streetscapes linked to the town's periods as royal center, missionary outpost, and whaling port.

thingsToDo.title: Banyan Tree Park
thingsToDo.description: Banyan Tree Park contains a large Ficus benghalensis planted in 1873 and is one of Lahaina's best-known civic spaces near the courthouse and harbor.

thingsToDo.title: Lahaina Harbor
thingsToDo.description: Lahaina Harbor is a small-boat harbor that historically supported shipping and now functions as an access point for inter-island and offshore marine routes.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Lahaina is on Maui's leeward coast and historically functioned as both a royal seat and a Pacific whaling port. The town developed around a protected shoreline used for shipping and fishing, with civic buildings concentrated near the waterfront. Historic district landmarks document nineteenth-century political and commercial periods. Current travel planning centers on open historic areas, harbor access, and nearby West Maui coastal routes.
